title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). K is a field of finite type over Q and K̄ an algebraic closure, with Γ = Aut_K(K̄). A 'D-structure' (discrétification) on K̄ assigns to every algebraic curve X/K̄ of type (g,ν) a discrete subgroup of the profinite étale π_1(X), compatibly with everything. It is 'spéciale' if it comes from an embedding φ: K̄ → C. In that case Θ_φ(X) is the image of the topological π_1(X⊗_φ C) under the comparison isomorphism, which identifies its profinite completion with π_1^et(X). The previous page proves that any two special discretifications are conjugate under Γ.

This page.

(1) There is a canonical surjection Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄), φ ↦ Θ_φ. It is Γ-equivariant: Γ acts on Hom by φ ↦ φ∘γ and on Discspec by transport of structure.

(2) NB. Γ is transitive on Discspec ('à droite', by the previous Prop). It is in general NOT transitive on Hom(K̄,C). Indeed φ' = φ∘γ for some γ ∈ Γ iff (a) φ|K = φ'|K and (b) φ(K̄) = φ'(K̄); then γ = φ^{-1}∘φ'. These conditions are 'des plus draconiennes'. The marginal star seems to say transitivity on Hom holds only when K̄ = Q̄ (K algebraic over Q), hence an injectivity statement can only be hoped for there.

(3) Programme: around a discretification, construct 'transcendental' invariants living over K⊗_Q C, i.e. on the space of complex embeddings of K. Example: periods as local functions of φ.

(4) Question: can Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄) be injective, hence bijective? That is, is the datum (K, K̄, φ: K̄ → C), equivalently (K, φ_K), the same as the datum (K, K̄, Θ) with Θ = Θ_φ? Conclusion: bijectivity ⇒ K algebraic over Q. This is correct. A Γ-equivariant bijection onto a transitive Γ-set forces Γ to be transitive on Hom(K̄,C). If K is transcendental, embeddings of K into C have different restrictions and images, so transitivity fails.

(5) Next idea, about the transcendental data that Θ alone does not see. On π_1 and π_1^ab there is a mixed Hodge structure. π_1^ab⊗C gives (for compact curves) a complex structure on π_1^ab⊗R. This is the period/Hodge datum that depends on φ beyond the Z-lattice Θ_φ(X)^ab. So the page is groping toward: which part of the embedding φ is encoded by the Betti lattices (Θ), and which by Hodge data? The overall purpose (Teichmüller dossier) is to understand Γ acting on 'discretified' profinite fundamental groups, i.e. Betti structures inside étale π_1, as a bridge between Galois action and transcendental Teichmüller theory.
errors: The injectivity question, even for K = Q (K̄ = Q̄), has a negative answer as literally posed, because of complex conjugation. If c is complex conjugation, then X⊗_{c∘φ}C is the conjugate complex manifold, whose underlying topological space and coverings are the same as for X⊗_φ C. Hence Θ_{c∘φ} = Θ_φ. So the fibres of Hom(Q̄,C) → Discspec(Q̄) have at least 2 elements; the stabiliser of Θ_φ in Gal(Q̄/Q) contains φ^{-1}cφ. The page does not mention this. The correct question is whether the map is bijective modulo complex conjugation, i.e. whether Stab(Θ_φ) = {1, c_φ}.

The marginal note 'lorsque K̄ = Q̄' is only literally right for K = Q. For a number field K ≠ Q, Γ = Gal(Q̄/K) has [K:Q] orbits on Hom(Q̄,C), since φ|K varies. So transitivity on Hom requires K = Q, not merely K algebraic.

The chain of equivalences '(K, φ_K) i.e. ... équivalent à (K, K̄, Θ)' is only heuristic. A discretification can at best recover φ up to the relevant automorphisms (conjugation, and for transcendental K much more).

ideas.what: Discretification (D-structure) of a field K̄: a functorial choice of discrete 'Betti' subgroups inside étale π_1 of all curves over K̄; special ones induced by embeddings K̄ → C
ideas.modern_name: Betti structure / Betti realisation on profinite fundamental groups over an abstract algebraically closed field; comparison-isomorphism data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Comparison theorem: SGA1 (Grothendieck). The abstract notion of 'discrétification' as a structure on K̄: no standard attribution
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse in this form as far as I know; Esquisse discusses the discrete vs profinite Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Γ-equivariant surjection Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄); Γ transitive on Discspec but not on Hom; criterion for φ, φ' to be Γ-conjugate (same restriction to K and same image)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/orbit analysis of complex embeddings versus Betti structures

ideas.what: Bijectivity of Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄) forces K algebraic over Q
ideas.modern_name: Betti lattices cannot detect transcendental embedding data

ideas.what: Question: does the system of topological π_1's inside profinite π_1's of all curves over Q̄ determine the embedding Q̄ ⊂ C (up to complex conjugation)?
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser in G_Q of the discrete free group F_2 ⊂ F̂_2 (and of Betti lattices of all curves); 'Betti rigidity'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related facts appear around Belyi's theorem (1979), GT̂ (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara) and the discussion of complex conjugation in the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Galois action on the profinite tower and the role of complex conjugation, not this exact question

ideas.what: Transcendental invariants of a discretification as local functions on Hom(K,C) ~ K⊗_Q C; mixed Hodge structure on π_1, π_1^ab; complex structure on π_1^ab⊗R
ideas.modern_name: Period map / Hodge structures on H_1 and Hain–Morgan mixed Hodge structure on π_1; period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (MHS, 1971–74), Morgan (1978), Hain (1987); periods as functions of the embedding: Kontsevich–Zagier (2001)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's question, corrected for complex conjugation: for K = Q, is Hom(Q̄,C)/{conj} → Discspec(Q̄) bijective, i.e. is Stab_{G_Q}(Θ_φ) = {1, c_φ}? A plausible proof sketch follows. If σ preserves the discrete F_2 = π_1^top(P^1−{0,1,∞}) up to conjugacy, then on the abelianisation χ(σ) ∈ Ẑ* ∩ Z = {±1}. After composing with c we get χ = 1. Then σ acts by y ↦ f^{-1} y f with f in the profinite commutator subgroup, and the GT relations should force f = 1, giving σ = 1 by Belyi's faithfulness. The page states the question but neither notices the conjugation obstruction nor answers it.
missed.quote: Est-il possible que Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄) soit injectif (i.e. bijectif) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean 'Betti rigidity' statement: the discrete fundamental groups of curves, as subgroups of their profinite completions, pin down the complex embedding of Q̄ up to conjugation. It sits between Belyi/GT̂ theory and anabelian geometry. I am not aware of it being stated in exactly this functorial form, although its ingredients are known.

missed.claim: The notion of a general (non-special) discretification of K̄ and the problem of characterising the special ones, and of describing the fibres of φ ↦ Θ_φ for transcendental K, are left open. Recovering the remaining embedding data via Hodge/period invariants 'sur K⊗_Q C' is also left open.
missed.quote: Autour d'une discrétification sur K̄ : on construit d'invariants par des "le cas transcendant" sur K⊗_Q C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This connects to the period torsor and the motivic Galois group of periods (Kontsevich–Zagier), and to the question of which abstract 'Betti structures' on étale π_1 come from complex embeddings. That is a Betti analogue of the section conjecture.

missed.claim: Placing the Galois action on discrete subgroups of profinite π_1 (dessins/Teichmüller tower side) next to the mixed Hodge structure on π_1 (Hain–Morgan side), seen as two parts of the data of an embedding K → C.
missed.quote: π_1  π_{1ab} structure de Hodge mixte ... on a une structure complexe sur π_{1ab}⊗_Z R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a foreshadowing (1981) of the later interplay of GT, multiple zeta values and the Hodge/motivic fundamental group (Deligne–Ihara–Hain–Brown). The idea here is however only gestured at.

deep.surprise_reason: The concept of a 'discrétification' as a structure on an abstract algebraically closed field, and the clean question whether it determines the complex embedding, are an original and unpublished framing. The deduction on the page is elementary, though, and the question as posed overlooks complex conjugation. The Hodge remarks are only sketched.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note near 'transitif' probably reads '* sauf si [or: lorsque] K̄ = Q̄, i.e. (K alg. sur Q)'. The second marginal line likely reads 'donc l'injectivité [n'est envisageable que ...]'.
The inserted words above 'transcendants' look more like 'le cas' than '"local"', giving roughly 'des "le cas transcendant"'. This is uncertain.
The top-left marginal 'Soit ⊥' / 'Soit alors ||' is illegible checkmarks/brackets; it is not mathematical content.

The sentence after the question is a crossed-out/rerouted passage. Its sense seems to be that the data (K, K̄, φ_{K̄}: K̄ → C), i.e. (K, φ_K: K → C), and the data (K, K̄, Θ) with Θ = Θ_{φ_{K̄}} would be equivalent, which forces K algebraic over Q.
